notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Grounding for mint sites and occasions comes from reading src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.cs (CollectObligations, WalkExpression, WalkActions), ProofEngine.Analysis.cs, ProofEngine.Intervals.cs, the four requirement-declaring catalogs (Operations.cs, Functions.cs, Actions.cs, Types.cs), Action.cs (the DynamicObligationGenerator catalog field), TypeChecker.Expressions.AssignmentQualifiers.cs, and DeclaredPresence.cs — not from precept_compile, which per the corrected inputs is a syntax/compile oracle only. Where slice-3-boundary-report.md's own live-verified findings corroborate a source-reading conclusion, that is cited as corroboration, not as the ground truth itself.

1) FIVE KINDS HAVE NO CATALOG SITE, confirmed independently by an exhaustive grep of every `new <Kind>ProofRequirement(` construction across src/Precept/: Presence (ProofEngine.cs:374), IntervalContainment (ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:518,562 plus Actions.cs:460), LengthContainment (ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:481,671 plus Actions.cs:429), CountContainment (ProofEngine.cs:641, ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:703), AssignmentQualifier (TypeChecker.Expressions.AssignmentQualifiers.cs:208). This matches the corrected-input's own citation set and slice-3-boundary-report.md finding #1 (independently re-derived here, not copied).

2) NUMERIC HAS A SPLIT MINT IDENTITY. The dominant path is catalog-declared (BinaryOperationMeta/FunctionOverload/ActionMeta/TypeAccessor.ProofRequirements), but ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:627 (CollectNumericDefaultObligations) synthesizes additional Numeric obligations by reading the Modifiers catalog's ProofSatisfactions table (not a ProofRequirements slot) against a field/arg default literal. hasCatalogSite is recorded true for the kind as a whole because the majority of its mint sites are genuinely catalog-declared, but this default-value path is a second, engine-driven mechanism that a catalog-only enumeration would also miss — it is one of the seven dynamic mechanisms slice-3 named, independently reconfirmed here at its exact line.

3) THE DYNAMIC-GENERATOR HOOK IS CATALOG-REGISTERED BUT ITS OUTPUT IS SYNTHESIZED. IntervalContainment's and LengthContainment's write-site (non-default) obligations run through ActionMeta.DynamicObligationGenerator — a function-pointer field literally declared on the catalog (Action.cs:30/46, assigned at Actions.cs:76 for the Set action kind). The dispatch is catalog metadata; the obligation instance is built dynamically per field from GetFieldBounds/declared min/max, which is why hasCatalogSite is recorded false for both kinds — no catalog member declares a bound value or a ProofRequirement instance, only the fact that Set actions should run a generator at all. This is a real nuance a strict binary catalog/synthesized split loses, and is called out explicitly here per the corrected input's instruction to find the real mint sites rather than trust catalog-only vocabulary.

4) TEN EVALUATION POSITIONS ARE DEFINITIONALLY REQUIRED BUT MINT NOTHING AT HEAD (build gaps), independently confirmed here by reading CollectObligations/WalkActions/WalkExpression: TypedTransitionRow.Guard, TypedStateHook.Guard, TypedRule.Guard, and TypedEnsure.Guard are consulted only as discharge fact sources (GuardOfContext / ExtractGuardBranches), never passed to WalkExpression — so transition-row-guard, state-hook-guard, rule-activation-guard, and ensure-activation-guard mint nothing. TypedRule.Message / TypedEnsure.Message are never walked at all, so constraint-rationale-interpolation mints nothing. Most strikingly, CollectObligations's per-row dispatch is `if (row is TypedTransitionRowSuccess success) WalkActions(...)` (ProofEngine.cs:216-217) — TypedTransitionRowReject rows are never visited by any walk, so reject-message-interpolation is not under-walked, it is structurally unreachable in the current pipeline. This is the exact site want-doc:72 cites to argue the fault axis has to exist at all, so its absence from the mint surface is a first-order gap, not a minor one. These findings corroborate (via independent source-reading) rather than merely repeat slice-3-boundary-report.md finding #9's already-live-verified list. Representative GAP cells are recorded once per affected occasion (primitive family only) in the Numeric kind rather than crossed with every type family, since the disposition (nothing minted) does not vary by operand type; the same gap applies identically wherever these occasions would otherwise appear for Dimension/Modifier/QualifierCompatibility/QualifierChain/DimensionalProduct — omitted from those kinds' cell lists for space and flagged here rather than silently dropped.

5) TWO EVALUATION-SITE CATEGORIES ARE LEFT OUT OF EVERY KIND'S OCCASION LIST AS UNRESOLVED: type-qualifier-expression and collection-inner-type-modifier-value-expression. I could not determine, from source in the time available, which kind(s) if any actually construct a ProofRequirement at these positions, and slice-3-boundary-report.md independently recorded both as unmeasured (with the added confound that an undeclared reference in these positions produces zero diagnostics at HEAD, meaning the expression is not even type-checked there). field-modifier-value-expression is similarly left out for the same reason for every kind except where an engine-synthesized default/write-site path demonstrably reads a modifier's own declared bound (which is a different mechanism than walking a modifier's expression as a fault site).

6) access-mode-guard IS AN UNRESOLVED COORDINATE. No code path in ProofEngine.cs walks TypedAccessMode.Guard. I could not determine in this pass whether that is a deliberate scope exclusion (access-mode guards are a governance/type-checking concern, not a fault-proof site) or an eleventh build gap beyond slice-3's ten. Left out of every kind's occasions rather than guessed.

7) construction-row-action-operand IS AN UNRESOLVED COORDINATE. The ObligationContext DU (ProofLedger.cs:85-92) has exactly eight subtypes — TransitionRowContext, ConstraintContext, StateHookContext, EventHandlerContext, FieldExpressionContext, FieldDefaultContext, ArgDefaultContext — with no distinct construction-specific context. CollectObligations walks TransitionRows/EventHandlers/StateHooks/Rules/Ensures/computed-and-default expressions only; there is no separate construction-row pass. Whether construction fires through TransitionRowContext (an initial transition row) or EventHandlerContext (the initial event's own handler, structurally identical to a stateless handler) was not resolved against the parser/grammar in the time budget for this pass, even though the transport-rule-restatement doc's route table treats construction-row-action-operand and stateless-hook-action-operand as two distinct site categories. Left out of every kind's occasion list rather than asserted; flagged here as a genuine gap in this coordinate map, not a pruned-empty cell.

8) TYPE-FAMILY APPLICABILITY VERIFIED AGAINST DOC TEXT WHERE POSSIBLE: Presence applies to all four families per collection-types.md:779 ('optional | any field type (including collections)'). Choice (Modifier's only family) is documented in primitive-types.md, confirming primitive rather than business-domain. IntervalContainment's applicability to the temporal family (whether duration/period fields can carry declared min/max via a Numeric SelfValue ProofSatisfaction) is UNVERIFIED in this pass — GetFieldBounds (ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:332) is generic over any field carrying such a modifier satisfaction, but I did not check whether any temporal-lane modifier ever produces one; left out of IntervalContainment's typeFamilies rather than assumed, flagged here.

9) CELL-LIST COMPRESSION, STATED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENT. For Presence, whose obligation schema ('subject is-set') is provably invariant across the four type families (the family only changes which label the subject's type carries, never the schema's shape), the eight occasions are each paired with one representative family (cycled across all four) rather than the full 32-cell mechanical cross, to avoid 24 cells that would repeat an identical schema shape. For Numeric's six build-gap occasions, one primitive-family cell each is recorded rather than the full three/four-family cross, per point 4 above. Every other kind's cell list is the genuine full occasion x type-family cross for that kind's (typically narrow, 1-3 family) applicable set, with no compression.
